job.style: a step-by-step explanation of a process

passage: The Weimar Republic faced immense challenges after World War I, primarily due to the harsh Treaty of Versailles. To pay off massive war reparations, the government began printing paper currency recklessly, which led to hyperinflation and destroyed the savings of the middle class. While the Nazis later claimed they would restore Germany's glory, Hitler did not seize power through a military coup. Instead, he was appointed Chancellor in 1933 through the existing democratic framework. Once in control, the Nazi regime implemented the concept of 'Lebensraum,' which was not about building houses, but a geopolitical strategy to acquire new territories in the East for German expansion. Furthermore, the Nazis used deceptive language to hide their atrocities. They referred to the systematic mass murder of Jews as 'Special Treatment,' a cold euphemism meant to mask the reality of the gas chambers. Finally, the Nazi definition of 'Aryan' had nothing to do with religion; it was a pseudoscientific racial construct used to categorize people as 'superior' or 'inferior' based on biology, not faith. These policies were enforced through strict social control, ensuring that the regime's ideology permeated every aspect of German life.

items.evidence: To pay off massive war reparations, the government began printing paper currency recklessly, which led to hyperinflation and destroyed the savings of the middle class.
items.q: Germany's government prints huge amounts of new money to pay its debts. What happens to ordinary families?
options: Prices soar and their savings lose value
Their savings grow along with the new money
Their debts shrink and they become richer
Only banks lose, while families stay safe
items.explain: Reckless money printing caused hyperinflation, which destroyed the savings of the middle class.

wrong.why: thinks printing money is a good way to solve debt
thinks more money means more wealth for everyone
thinks only banks are hurt by inflation

items.evidence: While the Nazis later claimed they would restore Germany's glory, Hitler did not seize power through a military coup. Instead, he was appointed Chancellor in 1933 through the existing democratic framework.
items.q: How did Hitler come to hold the highest government office in 1933?
options: He was appointed through the legal system
He took over by force with his army
He won a war against the Weimar leaders
He was chosen by the Treaty of Versailles
items.explain: Hitler was appointed Chancellor in 1933 through the existing democratic framework, not by a military coup.

wrong.why: thinks Hitler seized power by a coup
thinks power was won through a civil war
mixes up the treaty with the cause of his rise

items.evidence: Once in control, the Nazi regime implemented the concept of 'Lebensraum,' which was not about building houses, but a geopolitical strategy to acquire new territories in the East for German expansion.
items.q: German families are told about Lebensraum. What did the Nazis actually want to do?
options: Take over lands in the East
Build new homes in German cities
items.explain: Lebensraum was a strategy to acquire new territories in the East for German expansion, not housing.

wrong.why: reads 'living space' as better village land
picks a peaceful meaning for expansion

items.evidence: They referred to the systematic mass murder of Jews as 'Special Treatment,' a cold euphemism meant to mask the reality of the gas chambers.
items.q: Why did the Nazis call mass murder 'Special Treatment'?
options: To hide the cruel truth of their acts
To give victims better care in camps
To show that the victims were honoured
To follow rules made by the Weimar Republic
items.explain: 'Special Treatment' was a euphemism meant to mask the reality of the gas chambers.

wrong.why: blames the Weimar Republic for Nazi policy
